Hjørring is a Danish municipality assessed in the 2022–2023 Annual Report from the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database, published by the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP) [^src1]. The report evaluates the quality of treatment for patients with atrial fibrillation, with a specific focus on anticoagulation therapy and its safety monitoring across all 98 Danish municipalities [^src1]. 

Hjørring is notable for its strong performance regarding Indicator 4b, which measures adherence to safety practices when using DOAC (Direct Oral Anticoagulant) medications [^src1]. The municipality successfully meets the required standard, achieving a compliance rate of 96.1% (1,347 out of 1,402 patients) [^src1]. This places Hjørring among the municipalities that exceed the national standard threshold of ≥95% [^src1]. 

Beyond Indicator 4b, the municipality is also tracked for other key clinical quality indicators, such as the early initiation of anticoagulation treatment and the prevention of ischemic strokes [^src2]. These metrics, derived from national registries like LPR and DanStroke, are broken down to the municipal level to facilitate local quality development and benchmarking within Denmark's decentralized healthcare system [^src2]. Hjørring's specific data points for these indicators are documented to monitor its ongoing clinical performance and ensure accountability in patient care [^src2].
